newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before PPI.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits narrowly mixed before PPI.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were narrowly mixed in thin trade, dealers said on Friday.
They said most traders were sidelined before today's issue of the U.S. March producer price index (PPI) and retail sales index (RSI) data.
The producer price index for March is forecast to be unchanged from a 0.4 percent decline reported in February.
The March retail sales index is expected to ease to 0.6 percent against February's 0.8 percent.
"Rates were narrowly mixed amid uncertainty over market direction," a local dealer said.

"There was little impact from Thursday's weekly jobless claims figures and most people are sitting on the sidelines. But some people are waiting for today's issue of the producer price index and retail sales index for March for fresh clues to market direction," he said.
"I don't think there will be much impact though, as the numbers have been built into the market and most people have squared or are squaring their positions for the weekend," he added.
In short dates, weekend and Monday/Tuesday eased 1/8 percentage point to a common 5-1/2 5-3/8 percent, respectively.
Among term rates, one-month was unchanged from Thursday's 5-11/16 5-9/16 percent, three-months unchanged at 5-13/16 5-11/16 and twelve-months unchanged at 6-5/16 6-3/16 percent.
